course_description:
This course aims to provide information and experiences that will prepare students for a support role in veterinary clinical practice by providing theory and practical skills in the fields of small animal clinical practice.

This course will develop student knowledge, skills and expertise essential for the successful performance of veterinary technologists in clinical practice. Emphasis will be placed on methods of nursing practice, foundations of anaesthesia, surgery and wound management, radiography, dentistry, general medicine, physiotherapy, clinical nutrition, oncology and avian/exotics care pertaining to the veterinary technician.

learning_outcomes.description: Safely and competently restrain and examine healthy, injured and diseased animals, including domestic and exotic species, and fauna.

Demonstrate appropriate knowledge and identify skills applicable to veterinary technology and nursing practice in the context of well, injured, and diseased animals across the fields of anaesthesia, surgery, radiography, dentistry, general medicine, physiotherapy, clinical nutrition, oncology and avian/exotics care.
Demonstrate an appropriate level of competency in all aspects of surgical nursing, including asepsis, patient preparation, personnel preparation/management, and instrumentation.
Work with colleagues as a team to communicate concepts and accomplish shared goals and reflect on the performance of team members.

assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Time limited. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The Veterinary Terminology Workbook introduces students to a range of terms relevant to veterinary technology and nursing in a contextualised format. Objectives: By the end of this task, students should be able to: Identify prefixes, suffixes and roots that make up common veterinary medical terms Demonstrate an understanding of a variety of basic veterinary medical terms Appreciate the importance of learning medical terminology for employment within the veterinary and allied animal health industries Instructions: Students will be given an online Terminology Workbook at the start of the semester and are required to work through each of the TEN (10) Sections, completing TWO (2) sections each week (or by Week 6 at the latest). To complete this task, students will need to refer to the online notes provided on Blackboard. An in-person, online, In-Semester Exam will be scheduled - further details of this exam will be made available on Bb and discussed during Week 1. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Individual and Team-Based Learning Series
assessment_details.due_date: Anaesthesia TBL 2/09/2026 Radiology TBL 14/10/2026 Avian & Exotics TBL 20/10/2026
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Peer assessment factor. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Students are required to attend and engage in 3 TBL Assessments. TBL 1: Anaesthesia (5%) In-class assessment of engagement and completion of individual and group tasks. Students will complete an individual quiz based on course content. Students will then work in groups to undertake a second quiz. Marks will be an average of the individual and group quiz results. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. TBL 2: Radiography ( 5%) In-class assessment of engagement and completion of individual and group tasks. Students will complete an individual quiz based on course content. Students will then work in groups to undertake a series of patient positioning techniques that allow for radiographs to be taken effectively, this will culminate in a group assessment of ONE (1) position, chosen at random for each group. Marks will be an average of the individual quiz result and group activity results. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. TBL 3: Avian & Exotic Patient Care (5%) In-class assessment of engagement and completion of group task. Students will work in groups to create an information sheet that can be provided to hypothetical pet owners covering an assigned disease, its impact on husbandry, behaviour, nutrition and ways to improve their avian or exotic pets' health. Groups will be allocated randomly on the day of the Workshop. Assessment of this task will include peer evaluation of in-group engagement. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Students with acceptable reasons (medical or compassionate reasons or as a result of exceptional circumstances) may apply for an extension of the deadline. Information on applying for an extension can be found here: my.UQ Applying for an extension .
Extension applications must be received by the assessment due date and time.
NOTE: If an application for extension of assessment for TBL 1 or 2 is approved, the students grade for the task will consist entirely of their individual quiz mark.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
You are required to submit assessable items on time.
If you fail to meet the submission deadline for any assessment item, then 10% of the maximum possible mark for the assessment item (assessment ‘marked from’ value) will be deducted as a late penalty for every day (or part day) late after the due date.
For example: If you submit your assignment 1 hour late, you will be penalised 10%; if your assignment is 24.5 hours late, you will be penalised 20% (because it is late by one 24-hour period plus part of another 24-hour period).
10% will be deducted per day, for up to 7 calendar days, at which point your submission will receive a mark of zero (0) unless an extension has been approved.
NOTE: If an application for extension of assessment for TBL 1 or 2 is approved, the students grade for the task will consist entirely of their individual quiz mark.

assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This is an Objective Structured Clinical Examination based on course content designed to assess students' ability to perform various clinical and technical tasks. This will be held in the Centrally Scheduled Exam Pariod. Students will progress through a number of stations where they will be required to perform tasks and demonstrate skills taught/acquired in their practical classes. Students may also be expected to answer questions related to the task being examined in written or verbal form. All students will be examined on the same day. Assessed tasks may include: Behaviour, handling and restraint Clinical exam Catheter placement (model) Blood Draw (model) Preparing patients for surgery Dentistry (model) Instruments (dentistry & surgery) PALACE - R (radiography) Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 9 (27 Jul - 27 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Methods of Nursing Practice for the Veterinary Technologist - Lecture Series A series of lectures covering foundations of nursing methods, anaesthesia, radiology, care of the surgical patient (including detailed explanations of various surgical procedures), wound management and care.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 9 (03 Aug - 27 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Methods of Nursing Practice for the Veterinary Technologist - Practical Series Wound Management and Care Practical: Includes practical sessions on surgical preparation of wounds and bandaging of limbs in dogs/cats/horses/livestock. IV Catheter Placement and Blood Draw Practical: Using models students will increase skills using muscle memory to place catheters and complete blood draws. Escape Rooms: An interactive Team-Based learning experience that draws on knowledge and skills from the lecture series.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 3 To Week 13 (10 Aug - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Para-Veterinary Disciplines - Practical Series Physiotherapy Practical: students will learn to apply the theory of physiotherapy modalities to companion animals. Dentistry Practical: using models, students will increase their skills in charting, scaling and cleaning in companion animal patients. Nutrition Applied Case Practical: students will be emersed in case-based companion animal nutrition scenarios.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 4 To Week 12 (17 Aug - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Para-Veterinary Disciplines - Lecture Series Para-Veterinary Lecture Series: builds knowledge and skills in the para-veterinary disciplines of fluid therapy, dentistry, oncology, clinical nutrition and physiotherapy.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 7 To Week 13 (07 Sep - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Avian and Exotics - Lecture Series Avian and Exotics Lecture Series: builds knowledge and skills in reptile, avian, mammal and native fauna nursing.
